subject: MockMLDSAVerifier

artifactManifest.notes: bytecodeHash is keccak256 of the live runtime bytecode with the trailing 43-byte solc CBOR metadata region zeroed out (executableBytecodeMatch covers this same normalized region). MockMLDSAVerifier has no `immutable` variables and no constructor arguments, so no immutable-slot verification applies. Verified from a clean `npm ci` + `npx hardhat compile` in a worktree pinned to the deployment commit (Hardhat 2 / solc 0.8.24+commit.e11b9ed9, optimizer runs=200, evmVersion=cancun) against the live Sepolia runtime read via eth_getCode; independently cross-checked with a second solc build variant (solc-js/WASM) to rule out a compiler-binary cause for the metadata divergence.

disclosures: TESTNET ONLY — Ethereum Sepolia. Research prototype. Not audited. No production security guarantee. Do not use real funds.

This is a MOCK verifier. It performs structural length/shape checks only — it does NOT verify a real ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204 / Dilithium3) lattice signature on-chain. A passing result means 'structurally plausible', never 'cryptographically authorized'. See docs/Verifier_Roadmap.md.

All executable runtime bytecode was independently recompiled from public commit 35c25fa294bebea44b3089aa2435a190a5adf3fb (tag v0.4.24) and matched the live Sepolia deployment exactly. Only the trailing 43-byte solc CBOR metadata hash — a non-executed IPFS content pointer, never run by the EVM — differs, consistent with a build-environment difference (OS/toolchain/path) rather than a source or code difference; it is not claimed to match and does not affect on-chain behavior.
No Ethereum mainnet deployment of this contract exists or is planned.
